solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ex-president agitated State Department, ultimately in a spot

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: James K. Polk, eleventh US president
an ado is a fuss, an agitated state

explanation.surface: A former president, rattled by the State Department, finds himself in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a spot' reads as 'in trouble', but 'in' only joins and 'a spot' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A polka dot is one of the round spots printed in a regular pattern on fabric.

clue.text: Working business boss recalled minister's survey

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: on as in switched on, working
short for reverend, a minister of religion

explanation.surface: An executive brought back a government minister's report.
explanation.walkthrough: The minister is a clergyman, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a quick look or inspection, a brief survey.

clue.text: Nursery rhymes for Linda Barton

indicators.note: a rhyme for a word swaps its opening sound and keeps the rest

blocks.note: a rhyme for Linda, its opening L swapped for K
a rhyme for Barton, its opening B swapped for G

explanation.surface: Nursery rhymes written for a child called Linda Barton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursery rhymes' reads as a phrase, but 'Nursery' is the definition and 'rhymes for' tells you to find words that rhyme with the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindergarten is a nursery school for young children.

clue.text: Tattoo is funny peculiar, with funny ha-ha edging

indicators.note: edging means forming a border round, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: rum is old British slang for odd

explanation.surface: Getting a tattoo is strange, with some comedy round the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny peculiar or funny ha-ha?' is an English idiom separating the two senses of funny. A tattoo is a drumbeat as well as skin art.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic drumbeat, so a drum roll is a fair equivalent.

clue.text: Counter manoeuvres leading to defeat

indicators.note: manoeuvres means moves around, so the letters are repositioned

explanation.surface: Tactics to counter the enemy end in their rout.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat heavily and decisively.

clue.text: Big star's key song

blocks.note: the Alt key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A celebrity's signature tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The big star is in the sky, not on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is a bright star in the constellation Aquila, one of the brightest in the night sky.

clue.text: The Gunners fixing a day where young players train

indicators.note: fixing means rearranging, as in fixing a result, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Arsenal, nicknamed the Gunners, arranging a day at their youth training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is Arsenal football club's nickname, but here it is the Royal Artillery. RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London.
explanation.definitionFit: RADA is the London drama school where young actors train.

clue.text: Marcel Proust, say, has tea with these bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Proust takes tea with these fruits, a nod to his famous madeleine.
explanation.definitionFit: Proust, a refined lover of art and beauty, is an example of an aesthete.

clue.text: Drop in pace limiting English cricket side

indicators.note: limiting means hemming in, so one word holds the others inside it

blocks.note: the leg side of a cricket field, the side behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: A drop in pace keeps an English cricket team from winning.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side (or on side) is one half of a cricket field, split by the batsman's stance.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate a team is to drop it to a lower division.

clue.text: Sonnet's opening is able to follow a metrical pattern

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so take just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sonnet's first line manages to keep to its metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse that scans keeps correctly to the stresses of its metre.

clue.text: Guy known for storytelling amuses Pat and Dicky

indicators.note: dicky means faulty or shaky, so the letters before it are out of order

explanation.surface: A storyteller called Guy entertains his two friends Pat and Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a third name alongside Pat, but it is the British adjective for unsound. Guy de Maupassant was the French short-story master.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy de Maupassant was a nineteenth-century French writer famed for his short stories.

clue.text: Loudly quote drama during grand musical performance

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An actor declaims a line during a grand musical show.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight-playing is performing music at first sight of the score, without rehearsal.

clue.text: Poetry, finally moving, needs love really

indicators.note: the final letter moves, travelling round to the front of the word

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, a round O

explanation.surface: To be truly moving at the end, a poem needs love.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is an informal intensifier meaning very or really, as in 'ever so kind'.

clue.text: Jokester willing to show patience?

blocks.note: a card is a joker, a funny person
game means willing, up for it

explanation.surface: A prankster prepared to show forbearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is the British name for solitaire, so the question mark flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience (solitaire in America) is an example of a one-player game played with a pack of cards.

clue.text: Altered ground on which you might step

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remixed

explanation.surface: Changed land, somewhere you might put your foot down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered ground' reads as land that has been changed; 'ground' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever, as on an old sewing machine, that you press with your foot.

clue.text: Bail criminal in fix or jam

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are bent out of order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to tack is to fix, as with a small nail

explanation.surface: A criminal on bail finds himself in a fix, or a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' and 'jam' both look like trouble, but only 'jam' defines, as a traffic jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailback is a long queue of traffic, a traffic jam.

clue.text: Climber may want this coffee mostly sweet

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an ice is a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: A mountaineer might crave a coffee and something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The climber is a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice or trellis gives a climbing plant a framework to grow up.

clue.text: American backer I turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means flipped upward, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a show
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An American investor says he arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a native of Los Angeles, so an American.

clue.text: One on board ship wearing cape — a tough guy

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one piece is clothed by the other

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
a he-man is a macho fellow

explanation.surface: A crew member aboard ship in a cape, a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessman is a piece that stands on a chessboard.

clue.text: Checking time to visit Maxim

indicators.note: to visit is to go inside, so one letter is placed within the word

explanation.surface: Seeing when it's convenient to call on a man named Maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying a process means halting or checking it, as in staying an execution.

clue.text: I'm going to restaurant, admitting drug abuse

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: I'll is short for I will, I'm going to
a trat is a trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone heads for a restaurant and confesses to taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat someone is to abuse or mistreat them.

clue.text: Learner pilot follows men initially going for spin together

indicators.note: the first letter goes, leaving the rest of the word

blocks.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot

explanation.surface: A trainee pilot trails the men first heading off for a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the learner and pilot after the shortened men. 'Going for a spin' reads like a drive, but 'spin together' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlace is to entwine or wind together, as threads are spun together.

clue.text: Travel with convict, wanting one driver, say

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: a prisoner serving a life sentence
Roman numeral one, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A getaway trip with a jailbird who needs someone to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: A driver is a golf club as well as a motorist, and the 'say' warns the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer is someone who uses a driver, the club for long tee shots.

clue.text: Devotion to firm British monarchs defending country with displaced leader

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so one piece sits inside another
the leading letter is displaced, shifted from the front to the back

explanation.surface: British kings and queens defend a nation whose ruler has been ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand loyalty is a customer's habit of sticking with one company's products.

clue.text: The heart's gone out of market place in India

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, and it has gone, so remove it

blocks.note: an agora was the market square of an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: An Indian bazaar has become a soulless place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Market place' reads as one word, but 'place in India' is the definition and 'market' alone the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in northern India, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: E.g. compare or contrast the setter with a doctor

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as I
Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: An instruction to set the compiler side by side with a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Compare and contrast (the verb) are each stressed on the second syllable, so each is an example of the metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of an unstressed then stressed syllable, the pattern of com-PARE.

clue.text: Maybe Napoleon thus features in my article

indicators.note: something that features in another appears within it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: Napoleon perhaps appears in this way in an article I wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but stands for the exclamation 'cor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was born on Corsica, so he is an example of a Corsican.

clue.text: English-heritage.org inaccessible? Girl has got into it

indicators.note: the girl has got into the run of text, sitting inside the words before

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of heritage through .org into inaccessible

explanation.surface: A girl finds the English Heritage website down but gets in anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: English Heritage looks after historic sites in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgina is a girl's given name.
